headline: New frameworks resolve isoform, spatial, and regulatory layers of gene expression
label: Transcriptomic Frameworks Across Scales
summary: Long-read, multi-slice spatial, and RBP-binding datasets now support models that separate coordinated expression programs from gene abundance.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational decomposition of expression and regulatory data into interpretable components. Several items target spatial transcriptomics: DeSPA uses linear mixed models to detect cross-state spatial pattern remodeling across multi-slice atlases, SORT applies matrix factorization with orthogonality and graph total variation to recover multilevel gene programs across patients, and InSTability scores per-spot clustering instability across random seeds in linear time. IsoGraph separates coordinated isoform usage from gene abundance and is applied to aging human brain, while EpiFLAIR links single-molecule nucleosome states to isoform-level transcriptional fidelity in yeast ISW1/CHD1 mutants. Pythia provides structure-aware RBP-RNA binding prediction on the ecCLIP atlas of 67 RBPs. Swap-seq and ANeR extend the scope to deletion-based regulatory element mapping and translational fingerprints of M-phase. The items are heterogeneous in method and data type, and the shared contribution is the separation of components that a single readout would not resolve.
